title: Artlink First Fridays Art Walk
date: recurring: first Friday of every month
location: Roosevelt Row Arts District & Downtown Phoenix
address: Roosevelt Row, N Roosevelt St between Central Ave and 7th St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
description: The Valley's biggest free art crawl, running since the mid-'90s. Roughly 100 galleries, pop-ups, food trucks and street vendors spill across Roosevelt Row while the streets close to cars. Come thirsty and wear real shoes - it's a walking night, and even after sundown the pavement holds the day's heat.

title: Cactus League Spring Training
location: Various Cactus League ballparks across Greater Phoenix
address: Multiple stadiums, Greater Phoenix metro, AZ
description: Fifteen big-league clubs decamp to the Valley across ten ballparks, and the farthest drive between any two is about 45 minutes - so a doubleheader of stadiums in one day is genuinely doable. This is peak snowbird season, sun's out, tickets are cheap, and a lawn seat with sunscreen beats a Wrigley bleacher in April. Official 2027 dates drop from MLB in late 2026.

title: WM Phoenix Open
location: TPC Scottsdale (Scottsdale, just east of Phoenix)
address: TPC Scottsdale, 17020 N Hayden Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85255
description: The self-proclaimed Greatest Show on Grass, and the loudest hole in professional golf - the stadium-seated par-3 16th is a beer-soaked coliseum. It's technically over the Scottsdale line, but half the Valley shows up. Over 500,000 fans across the week; go early, hydrate, and pace yourself for the 16th.

title: Las Noches de las Luminarias
address: Desert Botanical Garden, 1201 N Galvin Pkwy, Phoenix, AZ 85008
description: Thousands of hand-lit luminaria bags line the desert trails while the saguaros glow and live music drifts through the cactus. This is the one night the desert asks you to bring a jacket - the Sonoran gives back the day's heat fast once the sun's gone. Timed entry, reservations required, and worth every reserved minute.

title: Devour Culinary Classic
address: Desert Botanical Garden, 1201 N Galvin Pkwy, Phoenix, AZ 85008
description: The Valley's chefs put Arizona on the culinary map here, and once a year they set up booths along the Garden's desert trails so you can graze and sip your way through the best local kitchens, breweries and distilleries. Eat in the shade of the cactus, and remember: the desert sun makes wine hit harder than you'd expect.

title: Downtown Phoenix Farmers Market
address: Arizona Center, 455 N 3rd St, Phoenix, AZ 85004
description: Rain or shine - though out here shine is the safe bet - 80 to 130 local growers and makers set up downtown every Saturday. In summer the market opens at 7:30 for a reason: shop early, before the pavement turns into a griddle. Local citrus, desert honey, tamales and breakfast burritos aplenty.

title: Roosevelt Row Sunday Arts and Farmers Market
description: First Friday's mellow cousin - a Sunday-morning mix of local produce, handmade goods and RoRo's resident artists, minus the crush of 20,000 people. A slow, shaded way to take the pulse of the arts district. Come before noon; by afternoon the district's gone quiet and the sun's gone unfriendly.

title: Festivin Winter Wine Festival
address: Wrigley Mansion, 2501 E Telawa Trail, Phoenix, AZ 85016
description: A European-style winter wine festival staged at the old Wrigley chewing-gum fortune's hilltop mansion, overlooking the Biltmore corridor. January in Phoenix is the good stuff - 70 degrees and a glass of something on a terrace while the rest of the country shovels snow. This is exactly why the snowbirds come.

title: Rock 'n' Roll Running Series Arizona
address: Race routes through Tempe and Phoenix, AZ
description: A marathon weekend with live bands staged along the course, run in January precisely because that's when the Valley's weather is a gift rather than a hazard. Try running this same route in July and you'd understand why every local race is scheduled for winter. Cool mornings, flat and fast, bands at every mile.

title: Arizona State Fair
address: Arizona State Fairgrounds, 1826 W McDowell Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85007
description: A month of fried everything, midway rides, livestock and Coliseum concerts under this year's 'A State of Wonder' theme. October is when the desert finally exhales and evenings turn pleasant - the fair opens Thursdays through Sundays, and dusk is the sweet spot before the funnel cake and the Ferris wheel.

title: MIKIZTLI: Dia de los Muertos PHX Festival
address: Steele Indian School Park, 300 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
description: The Cultural Coalition's long-running Day of the Dead festival - Aztec dance, masked performers, an artists' mercado, kids' art and a candlelit closing procession. This is the living heartbeat of the same Mexican-Phoenix culture that painted the Calle 16 murals and built the Barrio Cafe lineage. Bring marigolds and a memory.

title: Phoenix Pride Festival & Parade
time: Sat 2:00 - 10:00 PM; Sun parade 10:00 AM, festival 12:00 - 9:00 PM
address: Steele Indian School Park, 300 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
description: One of the Southwest's largest Pride celebrations, drawing 55,000-plus to Steele Indian School Park for headliners across multiple stages, with Sunday's parade marching down 3rd Street. Held in October once the heat breaks. Confirm the 2026 dates on phoenixpride.org before you book - the org is navigating a restructuring but says the festival goes on.

title: M3F Festival (McDowell Mountain Music Festival)
address: Steele Indian School Park, 300 E Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85012
description: A nonprofit, ad-free music festival that donates 100% of its proceeds to charity - two days of indie, electronic and jam acts in the middle of the city. Early March is prime Valley weather, so it draws the spring-training crowd looking for a night off from baseball. Rare thing: a festival with a conscience and a killer lineup.
